rules.description: The 3/10 oscillator is positive: the fast simple average of close is above the slow one. The standing state read of Grimes's zero line, as opposed to the cross event.

complexity.reason: two fresh Averages and a sign test

catalog_match.note: that rule fires only on the bar the two averages cross, using EL's `crosses` state machine; this is the standing state, true on every bar the fast average is above the slow one

rules.merge_notes: The settled oscillator form: Average(close, 3) - Average(close, 10), simple averages, never the MACD word. G16-11's exponential restatement loses to Appendix B's explicit SMAs. G07-23's setup is this rule NEGATED, ANDed in a pane with OscillatorSlowLineAboveThreshold.

rules.description: The 3/10 oscillator reaches a new oscLookback-bar high (long) / low (short) — a genuine momentum extreme, which Grimes uses to mark the pullback that follows as worth buying.
rules.pseudocode: osc[0] >= highest(osc, oscLookback)[1]   where osc[k] = average(close, fastLen)[k] - average(close, slowLen)[k]

complexity.reason: a Highest over a DERIVED series, so the oscillator's own history must be mirrored as a zero-seeded ring buffer (AwesomeOscillatorSlope and AtrRising are the precedents)

catalog_match.note: AwesomeOscillatorSlope carries the ring-buffer machinery but tests a slope of a different oscillator; no catalog rule takes an extreme of a derived momentum series

rules.merge_notes: One test at two lookbacks: G07-11 gives the book's stated 40-bar starting point, G03-12 guessed 20. Highest over an EL VARIABLE reads zero-filled warm-up history, so the long side passes trivially for the first oscLookback bars unless the rule guards on the bar counter.

rules.description: The 3/10 oscillator's current value ranks in the top fraction of its own oscLookback-bar history (long) / the bottom fraction (short) — Grimes's 'the fast line is extended', which he uses NEGATED to hold off an entry.

complexity.reason: a rank scan over the mirrored oscillator history, about the cost of a Highest

catalog_match.note: the same rank machinery on the oscillator instead of on close; that rule's own note (at rank ~100/N it degenerates to Breakout) is the precedent for keeping rank and extreme apart

rules.merge_notes: Kept apart from OscillatorNewExtreme on the ClosePercentileRank / Breakout precedent: a decile band and a window maximum are different bars, and this one degenerates to that rule only at the top rank. EL's Percentile over a variable reads zero-filled warm-up history.

rules.description: The 3/10 oscillator hooks up on this bar's close: it was flat or falling and is now rising (the mirror hooks down). Grimes's most responsive read — Appendix B shows the turn lands on the first bar of the new move.

complexity.reason: a bare offset comparison, but on the derived oscillator series, so its history must be mirrored

catalog_match.note: same family — the direction of a two-average oscillator — but a different series ((H+L)/2 vs close), different lengths, and an INFLECTION (a turn) rather than a lagged level comparison, so it fires on far fewer bars

rules.merge_notes: Two statements of one test; Appendix B (G14-03) adds only the synthetic-data proof that the hook fires on the new trend's first bar. The `<=` on the prior bar is deliberate: a flat-then-up turn counts.

rules.description: The 3/10 oscillator's slow line — a 16-period simple average of the fast line — is above thresholdAtr ATRs (long) / below minus that (short). At the default 0 this is Grimes's plain 'slow line above zero' trend confirmation; raised, it is his 'the slow line is extended'.

complexity.reason: an Average of a derived series (so the oscillator's history is mirrored), plus an ATR for the threshold

catalog_match.note: no catalog rule reads a signal line of a derived oscillator; AwesomeOscillatorSlope is the nearest derived-series machinery

rules.merge_notes: G14-02 gives the definition (16-period simple average of the fast line), G07-22 the zero read; G07-21's 'extended' read is the same test at a raised threshold, so it is one rule with thresholdAtr. The oscillator is a difference of averages of one series, so the zero test passes the shift test.

rules.description: Blocks the entry when the 3/10 slow line is extended beyond thresholdAtr ATRs AND has just turned back toward zero — Grimes's 'be suspicious of trades that set up against the slope of an extended slow line'.
rules.pseudocode: NOT( average(osc, signalLen)[0] > thresholdAtr * atr(atrLength)[0] AND average(osc, signalLen)[0] < average(osc, signalLen)[1] )

complexity.reason: the slow line plus a one-bar slope read; the negation is what forces it to be one rule

catalog_match.note: cited for the shape, not the content: that rule is the corpus's precedent for carrying a NOT(A AND B) blocker whole because ANDed panes cannot rebuild an OR

rules.merge_notes: Kept whole because Grimes states it negated: NOT(extended AND turning down) is an OR of two negations, which the pane system cannot assemble. Extension is in ATRs because the book gives no absolute level; 1.5 chosen.

rules.description: Some bar in the last withinBars moved the 3/10 oscillator by more than climaxMult times its own recent average bar-over-bar change — an indicator distortion from a climactic price move, after which Grimes says to disregard the oscillator.
rules.pseudocode: countIf( abs(osc[k] - osc[k+1]) > climaxMult * average(abs(osc - osc[1]), climaxLookback)[k], withinBars ) >= 1

complexity.reason: an Average of the absolute first difference of the oscillator, plus a short window scan; all over the mirrored oscillator history

catalog_match.note: the catalog's outsized-move tests (LargeRangeBarInWindow, AtrAtExtreme) measure price, not a derived indicator's jump

rules.merge_notes: Regraded from the miner's research grade: the arithmetic is exact and only the constants are unstated, which is what optimizer inputs are for in this corpus. The book's cooldown is folded into withinBars. Identical both sides — a distortion carries no direction; Grimes uses it negated.

rules.description: Price has crossed the moving average at least maxCrosses times in the last lookback bars — chopping back and forth on both sides of it, which Grimes says is a market to move on from. Blocks entries on both sides.
rules.pseudocode: countIf( (close[k] > ema(close, maLength)[k]) <> (close[k+1] > ema(close, maLength)[k+1]), lookback ) >= maxCrosses

complexity.reason: the EMA's own lagged history must be mirrored (EmaSlope's ring buffer) so the sign of close-minus-average can be compared bar by bar across the window

catalog_match.note: same role and intent — a global 'this is chop, stand down' override — but measured by how often price crosses the average rather than by how tall the last N bars are; the two disagree on a wide, slow range and on a tight trending drift

rules.merge_notes: No book number for 'chopping back and forth'; 4 crosses in 20 bars chosen, both optimizer inputs. Same Switch divergence to record as TightRangeBlocksEntries: the generator's Switch also forces flat, which Grimes does not ask for — place it negated per pane instead if that matters.

rules.description: Leave the trend trade when price gives up the moving average: the close crosses to the wrong side of it (long exits below), or with useTouch set, the bar merely touches it.
rules.pseudocode: close[0] < ema(close, emaLength)[0]     // useTouch = 1: low[0] < ema(close, emaLength)[0]

complexity.reason: an EMA; reads no position state, so it is an exit by placement (ConsecutiveCloseExit's precedent)

catalog_match.note: same comparison in the Entry role; the corpus has no plain moving-average EXIT — TrailArmedAfterEmaCloseBreak only ARMS a trail on it and MovingAverageTarget is a countertrend profit target at the average

rules.merge_notes: Grimes states both readings in one sentence ('touches or, in some cases, closes below'), so they are one rule with a mode input, on the GapMidpointMeasuredMoveTarget / ThreePushPattern precedent for boolean modes. He calls the length choice arbitrary; 20 keeps it with the Keltner family.

rules.description: Grimes's standard-deviation spike: the bar's change from the prior close is at least sdMultiple standard deviations of the bar-to-bar close changes over the last lookback bars. Volatility-standardized, direction-agnostic.
rules.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - close[1]) >= sdMultiple * stdDev(close - close[1], lookback)[0]

complexity.reason: a StdDev over a derived difference series, so its history is mirrored as a zero-seeded ring buffer

catalog_match.note: same StdDev machinery and the same warm-up mirroring, but on the bar-to-bar close CHANGE rather than the high-low range, and with no mean term added to the band — different bars entirely

rules.merge_notes: Two statements of one indicator; chapter 8 gives the numbers (20 bars, 3 deviations) and the glossary only names it. EL's StdDev is the POPULATION form and, over a variable, reads zero-filled warm-up history — BarRangeAboveStd is the port to copy. Grimes's cross-market colour screen is out of scope.

rules.description: Kaufman's Efficiency Ratio is at least erThreshold: the net move over erLength bars divided by the total distance travelled, 0 for pure noise and 1 for an unbroken line. A directness-of-movement filter, identical both sides.
rules.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - close[erLength]) / (sum(abs(close[k] - close[k+1]), erLength) + epsilon) >= erThreshold

complexity.reason: a fresh loop over close differences and one division; no cross-bar state at all

catalog_match.note: the corpus's trendiness filters are AdxBelowThreshold and the bar-overlap family; none measures net move against distance travelled

rules.merge_notes: Glossary-only. Grimes gives neither a length nor a cutoff, so both are optimizer inputs; 10 is Kaufman's own default and 0.3 a starting threshold. The epsilon guards the flat-market divide-by-zero, following CloseRangePosition. Differences only, so the shift test passes.
